title: Drooling Face Emoji 🤤 Meaning: Hungry or Thirsty?
description: The 🤤 drooling face means you want something badly: a plate of food, a new gadget or a person. See how the craving and flirty meanings differ in real texts.
summary: The 🤤 drooling face shows open desire for something. Most often that something is food, but it is just as commonly aimed at an attractive person, a car, a pair of sneakers or a vacation photo. The message is always the same: I want that, and I am not hiding it.
meaning: A line of drool running from the corner of a half-smiling mouth is cartoon shorthand for appetite, and that is how most people use 🤤. It lands under photos of ramen, in replies to someone describing what they are cooking, and in the group chat when a friend posts a dessert menu. It reads as a compliment to the cook and a mild complaint that you are not eating it yourself.

The second meaning is attraction. Sent in reply to a selfie, a gym photo or a celebrity post, 🤤 says the person looks good enough to drool over. It is blunt. Where 😍 says someone is lovely, 🤤 says something more physical, which is why it belongs to the family of emojis people describe as thirsty. Between partners it is playful; from a stranger it can feel like being stared at.

People also point it at objects. Car enthusiasts drop it under a clean engine bay, gamers under a new graphics card, and shoppers under a bag they cannot afford. Travel photos of clear water and empty beaches get the same treatment. In these cases there is nothing romantic about it. The drool just measures how much the sender wants the thing.

A smaller use is literal sleep. Because the eyes are closed or heavy on most designs, some people pair it with 😴 to describe a deep nap, the kind where you wake up with a wet pillow. Context makes this obvious, and it is far less common than the hungry or admiring readings.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Among friends 🤤 is nearly always about food. Someone says they are making tacos, you answer with 🤤 and an invitation is implied. It also works as a quick reaction to a photo of anything desirable, from a beach house to a new phone, without needing a sentence around it.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: If someone you are flirting with sends 🤤 after you post a photo, they are telling you they find you physically attractive, and they are not being subtle about it. It is a stronger signal than a heart or a fire emoji. Whether that is welcome depends entirely on how well you know each other.

contexts.label: On Instagram and TikTok
contexts.body: Food accounts collect this emoji by the hundreds. Recipe videos, cheese pulls and bakery reels fill up with 🤤 in the comments, often repeated three or four times. On thirst-trap posts the same emoji appears with a very different intent, usually alongside 🥵 or 🔥.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is fine when the subject is obviously lunch, such as a colleague sharing a photo of the team dinner. Aimed at a person or their appearance it is inappropriate in any professional channel, and even in food contexts some people find the drool itself a little gross.

examples.meaning: The sender is hungry just hearing about it and would happily be invited over.
A reaction to a food photo, praising how good it looks.
Flirty and direct: the sender finds the person in the photo very attractive.

examples.text: They just dropped the new colorway 🤤 my wallet is in danger
examples.meaning: The sender badly wants a product and is joking about buying it.
A literal use describing deep, drooling-on-the-pillow sleep.

combos.meaning: Craving a specific food; swap the pizza for whatever is on your mind.
Strong physical attraction to someone, usually in reply to a photo or video.
I have noticed this and I want it, used for both food and people.
Fast asleep and dead to the world, or looking forward to being so.

confusedWith.difference: 😋 licks its lips over food that tastes good and stays innocent. 🤤 is hungrier and less polite, and it stretches to people and objects in a way 😋 almost never does.

🥵 is flushed, sweating and panting, so it signals overheating or being overwhelmed by how attractive someone is. 🤤 expresses wanting rather than being overwhelmed, and it is the one people use for food.
😪 has a bubble at the nose, an anime convention for dozing. The liquid on 🤤 comes from the mouth and signals appetite, though both get used for sleep now and then.

avoid: Do not send it about a coworker's or stranger's appearance; it comes across as leering.
Skip it in reply to serious or sad news, where a hungry face makes no sense.
Think twice before using it on a first compliment to someone you barely know, since it is one of the more forward emojis.
design: A yellow face with relaxed, raised brows, a slack smile and a stream of saliva falling from one corner of the mouth. Some platforms draw the eyes closed in bliss and others leave them open and dreamy, which is the main difference you will notice between phones. The drool is blue or white depending on the vendor.

faqs.q: What does 🤤 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: When it is a reply to your photo, it means they think you look very attractive, and the meaning is the same regardless of who sends it. When it follows a mention of food, it only means they are hungry. Look at what the emoji is responding to.

faqs.q: Is the drooling face emoji flirty?
faqs.a: It can be. Aimed at a person it is one of the more openly lustful faces, closer to a wolf whistle than a compliment. Aimed at a burger it carries no flirtation at all. The ambiguity is small because the target is usually obvious.

Not on its own. It becomes inappropriate when directed at someone who has not invited that kind of attention, or in professional settings. For food, shopping and travel photos it is harmless and extremely common.

faqs.q: When was the drooling face emoji added?
faqs.a: It arrived with Unicode 9.0 in 2016, in the same release as the nauseated face, the sneezing face and the cowboy hat face. It has been available on all major platforms for years, so it displays reliably everywhere.
